curation_rule: Every fact needs a source. Summaries are in our own words. Record the highest determination actually reached, never a higher one.

cases.title: SyRI welfare fraud risk system
cases.deployer: Dutch government (Ministry of Social Affairs and Employment)
cases.summary: SyRI linked government data sets to score people for welfare fraud risk. Civil society groups challenged the law that allowed it.

determination.finding: The SyRI legislation breached Article 8 ECHR (private life). The court found its use insufficiently transparent and verifiable and declared the legislation to have no binding effect.

remediation.what: Legislation declared to have no binding effect.

sources.title: Rechtspraak: SyRI legislation in breach of European Convention on Human Rights
ASIL: Netherlands district court rules benefits fraud detection tool violates human rights

cases.title: South Wales Police live facial recognition (Bridges)
cases.summary: Police used automated facial recognition in public places to match faces against watchlists. A member of the public challenged its use.

determination.by: Court of Appeal of England and Wales
determination.finding: Use was not 'in accordance with the law' under Article 8 because too much was left to individual officers' discretion about who went on a watchlist and where it was deployed. The DPIA failed properly to assess the risks to data subjects. The court also held the force had not done enough to meet the public sector equality duty.

sources.title: Bridges v South Wales Police [2020] EWCA Civ 1058 (National Archives)

cases.title: Home Office visa application streaming tool
cases.summary: An algorithm sorted visa applications into risk streams, with nationality among its inputs. JCWI and Foxglove brought a judicial review in June 2020, alleging it was discriminatory.

determination.finding: No court finding. The Home Office suspended the tool pending a redesign and said it would consider the points raised, including unconscious bias and the use of nationality.

remediation.what: Interim process removed nationality as a streaming factor.

sources.title: Civil Service World: Home Office halts use of visa algorithm after legal challenge
UK Human Rights Blog: Government scraps immigration streaming tool before judicial review

cases.title: 2020 exam grading algorithm (England)
cases.summary: With exams cancelled, a statistical model standardised teacher-assessed A-level grades using schools' past results. Many students were downgraded, and the model was criticised for disadvantaging students at some schools.

determination.finding: No court finding. Grades reverted to centre assessment grades.

remediation.what: Model-standardised grades replaced by centre assessment grades.

sources.title: Leigh Day: Government announces u-turn over A-level grading
HEPI: The exams catastrophe, 16 questions that must still be answered

cases.title: Dutch childcare benefits: nationality data in fraud checks
cases.summary: In checking childcare allowance applications, the tax administration processed applicants' dual nationality data, including in a risk-classification model.

determination.finding: Processing of dual nationality data was unlawful, discriminatory and therefore improper, and the data should have been erased. Fined €2.75 million.

sources.title: IAPP: Dutch DPA fines tax authority 2.75M euros
Pinsent Masons Out-Law: Dutch tax authority record fine for discriminatory data processing

cases.title: Robodebt automated welfare debt recovery
cases.deployer: Australian Government (Centrelink / Department of Human Services)
cases.summary: An automated scheme raised welfare overpayment debts by averaging annual tax office income across fortnights, and left recipients to disprove the debts.

determination.by: Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme
determination.finding: Final report delivered 7 July 2023. Separately, the Federal Court approved a class action settlement in June 2021.

remediation.what: Class action settlement approved by the Federal Court: about A$1.2 billion in total, including A$112 million compensation.
Royal Commission final report and recommendations.

sources.title: Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme
HRLC: Federal Court approves $112 million settlement for the failures of the Robodebt system
